D35·d3hm — 2026-10-11
chose: 3.3 context packets, built as: three one-line packets rendered by core/packets.ts from facts already held (lease files, git, the fold), never a model, bounded (brief 800, notice 800, resume 1,600 chars), on a lanes run that leases only — `--leases off`, 3.4's naive arm, delivers none. LEASE NOTICE: in a lane session's opening prompt, every live lease another lane holds regions under; and at the lease hook, once per older holder and file, when an edit met none of that holder's regions (a steer in that file already named it otherwise). CHANGE BRIEF: read at each landing (git numstat, -U0 hunks mapped to the landed copy's sections and symbols by regions.ts spanRegions, one cat-file --batch), the D/M the task's sessions in this run logged (event ids by envelope session, numbered by fold position), the landing session's write-back; kept in the driver and appended to every other lease this run holds — the lease file doubles as the lane's inbox, opened without O_CREAT — said by that lane's hook once at its first edit of a file the landing changed; and listed under a conflicted merge's prompt for the landings it takes in (latest 3), as the other side's intent. RESUME PACKET: opens a lane session whose task a session of this run already handed off (park, failed check, merge conflict, stall): that session, how it ended, its write-back, the WIP (head, commits past the base, uncommitted paths), and after a park each waited lease's holder brief when it landed after the parked session launched, else that it let go.
over: Packets as record events (a schema change for something git and the record can re-derive; how cloud lanes, which cannot read the pool, get them is 4.3's to decide). A second per-lane inbox file (the lease already has exactly that lifetime and is already read on every edit). Regions from lease claims (what was claimed, not what landed, and nothing at all under --leases off). Every brief to every lane at its next tool call (tokens spent on files it never touches). Packets in the naive arm (would blur 3.4's comparison). A resume packet for parks only (a failed-check or merge-conflict retry would rediscover what the last session knew — D15's fresh-session-with-packet case).
because: The operator asked that once lane 1 finishes, the driver share it with lane 2 so lane 2 can write that file, and share context between lanes and the records — efficient and pre-engineered (brief 2026-10-10). Rendering from held facts keeps sofar at zero model calls and makes each packet byte-stable. Gating each delivery on relevance (the file being edited, the merge taking the landing in, the task coming back) means a lane pays roughly 100–400 tokens only where a packet bears on its next move, and the briefs cite D/M ids and write-backs that live in the record. 3.4 measures the whole conflict-aware arm against naive lanes.
